transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Hurst.
President Trump says on social media that there's an energy ceasefire between Russia
and Ukraine.
Ukrainian President Zelensky says he supports the idea but still doesn't have details,
and Russia hasn't commented, and here's Luke Garrett reports.
Early Sunday, Zelensky said he wanted to deal with Russia that would bar the two warring
nations from attacking oil and diesel infrastructure.
Here he is on ABC News.
We are ready for a ceasefire.
We are ready to begin from any kind of steps of escalation.
We are ready for energy ceasefire, not to attack energy both sides.
Zelensky then committed to holding Ukrainian elections if there's a 60-day ceasefire with
Russia.
Soon after, Trump announced an energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia "effective immediately."
But the deal has not been confirmed by Russia, and Zelensky says he and NATO Secretary General
Mark Ruta are still awaiting details on this deal between Russia and Ukraine.
Luke Garrett and Pierre News, the White House.
Democrats are turning to online influencers to win a lost electorate, Latino voters who
are frustrated with both parties.
And here's Claudia Garizalas reports House Democrats are kicking off a national tour
today with content creators in several swing districts.
The campaign arm of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus is fighting for Latino voters who deserted
Democrats in the 2024 elections, and haven't come back.
California Democratic Congresswoman Linda Sanchez, who chairs the group, says they're
asking content creators for help to bridge the gap.
We're turning to trusted voices in local communities that have followings, giving them information
and then allowing them to create content in a way that is organic and authentic.
Those get their political news from influencers more than any other demographic.
Content creators will join, get out the vote events in Colorado, Florida, New Mexico, Texas,
and Arizona.
Claudia Garizalas, NPR News.
Police in India freed the leaders of a movement that's calling for protests surrounding the
controversial revision of voter rolls, and Pierre's Dia Hadid reports it's the latest
political crisis to roil the government of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
The release of the three men came a day after they were removed from their airline seats
and detained by police just as their flight touched down in the capital.
They were among the thousands detained on Saturday as security forces tried to stave
off protests.
The forces barricaded parts of downtown Delhi, cut off the internet in parts of the city,
shut down metro stations, and banned gatherings.
Still, protests flared.
Demonstrators are demanding the resignation of the election commissioner after a revision
of voter rolls struck off more than 130 million people, or forced them to justify why they
should be allowed to stay on the rolls.
Pierre Hadid, NPR News, New Delhi.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Pope Leo says he's undergoing surgery to remove a nodule from his lung this week.
The 71-year-old says it's in the initial phase and localized, and he's expected to stay in
the hospital for about a week.
It's not clear if he still intends to take a scheduled trip to Uruguay, Argentina, and
Peru early next month.
It's pumpkin spice season, and some shoppers are paying a lot more for their fall-themed
products.
And, Pierre Stephen Bissaha reports, prices for pumpkin flavors cost more this year.
There's an almost 9% pumpkin spice premium, up a bit from last year.
Matt Schultz is chief consumer finance analyst at Lending Tree, which did the research.
He says some of the spooky season bump could be because pumpkins are slightly more expensive
this year, but also —
"Retailers understand how much people love pumpkin spice and how they might be willing
to pay a little bit extra for it."
Now, this does vary by store.
"If you take the time to look around at different places, you might be able to save yourself
a little money."
Out of the six retailers it looked at, Lending Tree says Starbucks and Trader Joe's had the
biggest fall-flavor hikes.
Stephen Bissaha, NPR News.
Egypt says a restored version of a second-century painting from the famous Phaeum portraits
will travel abroad for the first time.
Restoration work on the Tondo of the Two Brothers took three weeks, as they were usually painted
on thin wooden panels and placed over the faces of the dead with mummy wrappings.
The paintings will be on display temporarily in Rome starting next month.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Trump announces energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine; Zelensky and Russia await details
Democrats launch national tour with online content creators to win back Latino voters in swing districts
India police free protest leaders after detentions during voter roll revision protests in New Delhi
